# everpure_azure_reservation (Resource)

Manages a Reservation: the Everpure resource that storage pools in an Azure subscription and region are billed through. Creating a reservation purchases the Azure Marketplace offer named in `offer`; the reservation holds that purchase, and storage pools in the same region reference it through their `reservation_id`.

Creation is asynchronous and takes a few minutes.

Only one reservation can exist in an Azure subscription per region.

Every storage pool of the Azure subscription in that region, and everything stored in those pools, depends on the reservation. Protect it with `lifecycle { prevent_destroy = true }`, as the example does, so that no plan destroys or replaces it unnoticed.

~> **Destroying a reservation cancels its Marketplace purchase only if the purchase is managed through the reservation.** A purchase that exists as its own Azure resource, of type SaaS in the reservation's resource group, outlives the reservation and keeps billing until you delete that resource.

~> **A reservation can be imported, but its `user` is never read back.** `user` is write-only, so an imported reservation plans clean whether or not the configuration carries it.

Only `offer.plan_id` can be changed on an existing reservation. It changes the plan, and so the price, of the existing purchase in place; it is the same purchase afterwards.

## Example Usage

```terraform
terraform {
  required_providers {
    everpure = {
      source = "PureStorage-OpenConnect/everpure-azure"
    }
    azurerm = {
      source  = "hashicorp/azurerm"
      version = ">= 4.0"
    }
  }
}

# Credentials: `az login` by default, or the ARM_* environment variables /
# provider attributes described in the Authentication guide. The subscription
# can also be set via ARM_SUBSCRIPTION_ID.
provider "everpure" {
  subscription_id = var.subscription_id
}

provider "azurerm" {
  features {}
  subscription_id = var.subscription_id
}

variable "subscription_id" {
  type = string
}

variable "contact_email" {
  type        = string
  description = "Email address of the person responsible for the purchase."
}

resource "azurerm_resource_group" "example" {
  name     = "rg-storage-prod"
  location = "eastus2"
}

resource "everpure_azure_reservation" "example" {
  name                = "reservation-prod-east"
  resource_group_name = azurerm_resource_group.example.name
  location            = azurerm_resource_group.example.location

  # The Marketplace offer to purchase. Only plan_id can be changed in place.
  offer = {
    offer_id  = "krypton_3_plan"
    plan_id   = "psc_capacity_perf_ondemand"
    term_unit = "P1M"
  }

  # Write-only: sent when the reservation is created, never stored in the plan
  # or the state. Needs Terraform 1.11 or newer. Offers whose SaaS resource is
  # hidden reject a create without it.
  user = {
    first_name    = "Ada"
    last_name     = "Lovelace"
    email_address = var.contact_email

    company = {
      company_name = "Example Corp"
      address = {
        address_line1 = "1 Main Street"
        city          = "Seattle"
        state         = "WA"
        country       = "US"
        postal_code   = "98101"
      }
    }
  }

  tags = {
    environment = "prod"
  }

  # Destroying a reservation does not always cancel its Marketplace purchase,
  # and an Azure subscription can hold only one reservation per region. This
  # makes any plan that would destroy or replace the reservation fail.
  lifecycle {
    prevent_destroy = true
  }
}

# Storage pools reference the reservation.
output "reservation_id" {
  value = everpure_azure_reservation.example.id
}
```

## Schema

### Required

- `location` (String) Azure region the reservation is created in, using the canonical short name, e.g. `eastus2`. Storage pools require a reservation in the same region. Changing this forces a new reservation to be created.
- `name` (String) Name of the reservation. Changing this forces a new reservation to be created.
- `offer` (Attributes) The Azure Marketplace offer to purchase. Only `plan_id` can be changed in place; `offer_id` and `term_unit` cannot, because a different offer or term is a different purchase.

Offer and plan IDs are opaque strings that only the service judges: new offers and plans appear over time, and private plans exist per customer. The Everpure public offer on the Azure Marketplace is `krypton_3_plan`; its public plan with a monthly term is `psc_capacity_perf_ondemand`. The publisher is fixed and not configurable. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--offer))
- `resource_group_name` (String) Name of the resource group the reservation lives in. Changing this forces a new reservation to be created.

### Optional

> **NOTE**: [Write-only arguments](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/language/resources/ephemeral#write-only-arguments) are supported in Terraform 1.11 and later.

- `tags` (Map of String) A mapping of tags to assign to the reservation. Can be changed in place. Some environments append their own tags outside Terraform (e.g. an Azure Policy); including those tags in this configuration, or excluding them via a `lifecycle.ignore_changes` block, avoids a persistent diff against them.
- `timeouts` (Block, Optional) (see [below for nested schema](#nestedblock--timeouts))
- `user` (Attributes, [Write-only](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/language/resources/ephemeral#write-only-arguments)) Contact details for the purchase. Required by the service when creating a reservation; optional here only so that an imported reservation can be managed without it.

Write-only: sent on create, never stored in plan or state, and ignored if changed later. Needs Terraform 1.11 or newer. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--user))

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) The full Azure Resource Manager ID of the reservation, e.g. `/subscriptions/.../resourceGroups/.../providers/PureStorage.Block/reservations/res1`.
- `internal_id` (String) Everpure's internal ID of the reservation.
- `marketplace_subscription_id` (String) ID of the Azure Marketplace subscription that bills for the reservation.
- `marketplace_subscription_status` (String) Status of the Azure Marketplace purchase: `PendingFulfillmentStart`, `Subscribed`, `Suspended` or `Unsubscribed`. `Suspended` means the payment for the purchase is missing. The status can lag behind the purchase: it has read `PendingFulfillmentStart` on a purchase that was already activated, so do not wait for it to change.

<a id="nestedatt--offer"></a>
### Nested Schema for `offer`

Required:

- `offer_id` (String) ID of the Azure Marketplace offer to purchase, e.g. `krypton_3_plan`. An opaque string that only the service judges. Cannot be changed in place: a different offer is a different purchase.
- `plan_id` (String) ID of the offer's plan, e.g. `psc_capacity_perf_ondemand`. An opaque string that only the service judges. Can be changed in place, which changes the plan, and so the price, of the same purchase.
- `term_unit` (String) Length of the plan's billing term as an ISO 8601 duration, e.g. `P1M` (one month), `P1Y` or `P3Y`. Compared exactly as written: `P12M` and `P1Y` are different values, because Marketplace knows each term by one spelling. Which terms exist for a plan is for the service to say. Cannot be changed in place: a different term is a different purchase.

Read-Only:

- `plan_name` (String) Display name of the plan, as the service reports it. It is not set by every offer.


<a id="nestedblock--timeouts"></a>
### Nested Schema for `timeouts`

Optional:

- `create` (String) Defaults to 30 minutes. A duration string: a number with a unit suffix s (seconds), m (minutes) or h (hours); segments can be combined, e.g. "30m" or "1h30m". Used when creating the reservation.
- `delete` (String) Defaults to 30 minutes. A duration string: a number with a unit suffix s (seconds), m (minutes) or h (hours); segments can be combined, e.g. "30m" or "1h30m". Used when destroying the reservation.
- `read` (String) Defaults to 5 minutes. A duration string: a number with a unit suffix s (seconds), m (minutes) or h (hours); segments can be combined, e.g. "30m" or "1h30m". Used when reading the reservation.
- `update` (String) Defaults to 30 minutes. A duration string: a number with a unit suffix s (seconds), m (minutes) or h (hours); segments can be combined, e.g. "30m" or "1h30m". Used when updating the reservation.

### Nested Schema for `user`

Required:

- `first_name` (String, [Write-only](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/language/resources/ephemeral#write-only-arguments)) First name.
- `last_name` (String, [Write-only](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/language/resources/ephemeral#write-only-arguments)) Last name.

Optional:

- `company` (Attributes, [Write-only](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/language/resources/ephemeral#write-only-arguments)) The user's company. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--user--company))
- `phone_number` (String, [Write-only](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/language/resources/ephemeral#write-only-arguments)) Phone number.
- `upn` (String, [Write-only](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/language/resources/ephemeral#write-only-arguments)) Entra ID user principal name of the contact, e.g. `jane@contoso.com`.

<a id="nestedatt--user--company"></a>

Optional:

<a id="nestedatt--user--company--address"></a>
### Nested Schema for `user.company.address`

Required:

- `address_line1` (String, [Write-only](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/language/resources/ephemeral#write-only-arguments)) Address line 1.
- `city` (String, [Write-only](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/language/resources/ephemeral#write-only-arguments)) City.
- `country` (String, [Write-only](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/language/resources/ephemeral#write-only-arguments)) Country.
- `postal_code` (String, [Write-only](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/language/resources/ephemeral#write-only-arguments)) Postal code.
- `state` (String, [Write-only](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/language/resources/ephemeral#write-only-arguments)) State or province. Use an empty string where the country has none.

Optional:

- `address_line2` (String, [Write-only](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/language/resources/ephemeral#write-only-arguments)) Address line 2.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

In Terraform v1.12.0 and later, the [`import` block](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/language/import) can be used with the `identity` attribute, for example:

```terraform
import {
  to = everpure_azure_reservation.example
  identity = {
    subscription_id     = "00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000000"
    resource_group_name = "rg-storage-prod"
    name                = "reservation-prod-east"
  }
}

resource "everpure_azure_reservation" "example" {
  # ... configuration matching the imported reservation, including its offer
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
### Identity Schema

#### Required

- `name` (String) Name of the reservation.
- `resource_group_name` (String) Name of the resource group the resource lives in.
- `subscription_id` (String) Azure subscription ID the resource lives in.

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# Reservations are imported by their full Azure resource ID. The `user`
# attribute is write-only and is never read back, so it does not take part.
terraform import everpure_azure_reservation.example \
  "/subscriptions/00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000000/resourceGroups/rg-storage-prod/providers/PureStorage.Block/reservations/reservation-prod-east"
```
